title: io_callback does not work with custom_vjp
body: I want to save data to disk during the forward pass and reload it during the backward pass. I tried using io_callback inside custom_vjp forward and backward rules, but my implementation does not work. The example uses lax.scan for several forward steps and then computes a gradient.

symptoms_visible: My io_callback and custom_vjp implementation does not save and reload the data as I expect.
N0.label: N0 callback implementation reported

symptoms_visible: My io_callback and custom_vjp implementation does not save and reload the data as I expect.
N1.label: N1 custom VJP wiring problems identified

symptoms_visible: After adding custom VJP definitions around the forward and backward helpers, the expected tmp/x0.npy file is still not written.
N2_x.label: N2_x nested custom VJP attempt aftermath

symptoms_visible: My real inverse-problem workload cannot run when all of the forward residuals remain in GPU memory.
N2.label: N2 memory-management goal established

symptoms_visible: My workload is running on a GPU, and keeping the required residuals there causes an out-of-memory condition.
N3.label: N3 GPU transfer requirement established

symptoms_visible: After moving the custom-VJP residuals out of GPU memory during the forward pass and restoring them during the backward pass, my original GPU code uses less device memory and can run without the out-of-memory failure.
On my RTX 3090 workload it runs at about 3.7 seconds per iteration instead of 0.7 seconds, which is acceptable because the version without this change cannot run.
N_terminal.label: terminal residual storage method working

solution.intent: First correct the custom-VJP data flow: the differentiated computation must actually call the custom-VJP function, the forward rule must match the primal function's signature, and its residual output must contain what the backward rule expects.
solution.concrete_example: The opening loss only sums a value computed before value_and_grad traces the function, so it cannot invoke f's VJP rules. In addition, fwd accepts an extra cstep argument and returns None as its residual even though bwd tries to unpack x and cstep.
solution.inference_hint: These wiring errors are visible by tracing the pasted program: final_carry is computed outside cal_grad, f and fwd have different signatures, and fwd returns None where bwd expects a tuple.

edges.comment: From participant2 c1-c2, describing only the opening reporter's program. This is a prerequisite diagnosis, not the eventual memory-management solution.

solution.intent: Add nested custom-VJP definitions around the forward and backward helper functions so autodiff has rules around the locations that invoke io_callback.
solution.concrete_example: Define custom VJPs for fwd and bwd in addition to the outer custom VJP, and place the callback in fwd_fwd.

edges.comment: Reporter-only chain from participant1 c0, reporter c4, and participant1 c5. The reporter implemented nested custom VJPs, but the callback merely moved into fwd_fwd, which itself had no callback derivative rule, and the expected file still was not written.

question_patterns: What larger problem are you trying to solve with these callbacks?
Why do the forward-pass values need to be written to disk?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am working on full waveform inversion based on the wave equation. I run an iterative time-stepping forward scheme and compare its final result with a target.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I need the files as durable application output after the computation finishes; reducing accelerator memory is not the goal.
The temporary files can use any filename convention.

question_patterns: What data must be available to the backward pass?
Are these files ordinary outputs, or are they values needed to compute gradients?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: At each step my function uses several inputs such as x, y, and z. I need those values again during the backward pass so I can run jax.vjp and calculate the gradients.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The backward pass does not use the saved values at all; I only need an audit log of the forward values.
I need four wave-state arrays per step instead of three.

question_patterns: Is the goal to reduce GPU memory use or to persist the data permanently?
What failure occurs if you return the values normally?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The goal is to save GPU memory. If I retain the forward values normally, my inverse-problem code runs out of memory; disk was my idea for a checkpoint-like version.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: GPU memory is sufficient; the actual requirement is recovery after a process or machine restart.

edges.comment: From participant1 c5, reporter c6/c8, and participant3 c7. The larger full-waveform-inversion and OOM goal was elicited only after the nested-callback attempt failed.

question_patterns: Which accelerator hardware are you targeting?
Is this running on CPU, GPU, or TPU?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am coding and running this on a GPU.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: This must run on CPU-only machines, with no accelerator device memory involved.
I am using a different NVIDIA GPU model.

question_patterns: What happened when you tried jax.device_get on the values returned by the forward rule?
Can you show the code you tried with jax.device_get?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried returning (jax.device_get(x), jax.device_get(y)) from the forward rule, but I am not sure whether that makes sense under jit or how to determine the device of a DynamicJaxprTracer.

question_patterns: Does the operation need to work from inside the jitted custom VJP?
Is the custom-VJP function compiled with jit in your real code?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The custom-VJP function is jitted, so I need the transfer to work there rather than only converting an already-computed array in Python.

edges.comment: Reporter c10 supplies the GPU environment and device_get attempt. This remains on the original reporter's full-waveform-inversion chain; the later participant's transformer/remat problem is a separate deployment and is excluded.

solution.intent: Treat the files as backward residual storage rather than durable I/O: use jax.device_put with pinned-host memory in the custom-VJP forward rule, move the residuals back to device memory in the backward rule, and then compute the VJP from the reloaded values.
solution.concrete_example: In fwd, return the primal result and jax.device_put((x, y), SingleDeviceSharding(jax.devices()[0], memory_kind='pinned_host')). In bwd, use jax.device_put(res, SingleDeviceSharding(jax.devices()[0], memory_kind='device')), call jax.vjp(f, *reloaded_res), and apply the resulting VJP function to the incoming cotangent.
solution.inference_hint: Once the reporter explains that the files are only a way to reduce accelerator memory while retaining custom-VJP residuals, the engineer reframes the request as host-memory storage rather than persistent disk I/O. The reporter later confirms that the implementation reduces memory and permits the workload to run.

edges.comment: Accepted resolution from participant3 c9/c11 and reporter c12/c14. The reporter implemented the pinned-host device_put pattern in the original GPU inverse-problem code, confirmed reduced memory and avoidance of OOM, and accepted the approximately fivefold slowdown. Later comments c23-c28 concern another user's transformer/remat setup and are intentionally excluded.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the opening custom-VJP wiring problems: the differentiated loss does not trace through f_vjp, the forward rule's signature must match the primal function, and the forward residual must contain what the backward rule consumes.

Must recognize the final accepted diagnosis that the reporter's real requirement is GPU-memory reduction for backward residuals in an iterative full-waveform-inversion computation, not durable file output.
Must recommend offloading custom-VJP residuals with device_put to pinned-host memory in the forward rule and moving them back to device memory in the backward rule before computing the VJP.
Must not repeat the falsified nested-wrapper attempt that merely moves io_callback into another derivative-rule function without supplying a valid autodiff treatment for the callback.
Must mention the host-device transfer cost and ask the reporter to verify gradient correctness, reduced GPU memory use, and avoidance of OOM on the real GPU workload before declaring resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: New to JAX transformation semantics but technically capable in numerical computing; works on GPU-based full waveform inversion, can write custom VJPs, use lax.scan, benchmark code, and integrate a supplied memory-transfer pattern.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, cooperative, and code-focused; shares complete examples, explains the scientific workload when asked, reports concrete memory and timing outcomes, and accepts a slower solution when it makes an otherwise impossible workload run.
